<description>
**Problem:** With the `UnstableChain` IPC interface from #29409 merged, an IPC client could make `bitcoin-node` hit an `Assume` failure (debug builds) or compute wrong fees (release builds) by passing a malformed feerate to `broadcastTransaction`, `calculateIndividualBumpFees` or `calculateCombinedBumpFee`. These methods take feerates as serialized `Data` fields, and `CFeeRate` deserialization reads the fee and size without the checks its constructors do, so it accepts a negative size, which fee calculations require to be positive, and a zero size with a nonzero fee, which compares as an infinite feerate. Nothing deserializes a `CFeeRate` on master today.

**Solution:** Make `CFeeRate` deserialization throw on values its constructors cannot produce, the same way other malformed serialized data is rejected. The change is a `SER_READ` check in `src/policy/feerate.h` plus a unit test. It is similar to #36520, which handles other invalid arguments to `Chain` IPC methods.

This issue was found by Project Loupe and passed on by instagibbs.
</description>

<commits>
1c6060e7f6 policy: reject invalid CFeeRate values when deserializing

CFeeRate constructors turn a non-positive size into the empty feerate
{0, 0}, but Unserialize read fee and size from the stream unchecked.
A negative size then reaches FeeFrac::EvaluateFee, which requires a
positive size: debug builds hit an Assume failure, and release builds
compute wrong fees. A zero size with a nonzero fee compares as an
infinite feerate.

Nothing deserializes a CFeeRate on master, but the UnstableChain IPC
interface in #29409, used by the multiprocess wallet in #10102, passes
feerates as serialized Data fields, so an IPC client could send these
values.

Throw on values the constructors cannot produce, like other
deserialization errors.

This issue was found by Project Loupe and passed on by Greg Sanders.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5.
</commits>
